description: Somos un grupo de 6 personas con el interés de poder utilizar los datos que brinda la NASA para ayudar a un sector específico de la sociedad, a través de los cuales nos beneficiaremos todos.
summary: AGRONASA Climate-Smart Crop Planning for Farmers The problem Farmers must decide what to plant and when, often without access to reliable climate data or agronomic advice. Weather is increasingly unpredictable, and poor choices lead to water waste, soil degradation, erosion, and lost income. The solution AgroNasa is a free web tool that turns NASA data into practical, location-specific guidance. The farmer picks a plot on a satellite map, chooses a crop, and sets their priorities (saving water, improving soil, reducing erosion, or extra income). The app then:-  Compares recent rainfall, temperature, and soil moisture from NASA POWER against the historical average.-  Shows NASA GIBS satellite layers, with image dates.-  Rates the chosen crop's suitability and compares it with rotation alternatives, explaining the reasons, benefits, and risks.-  Calculates the crop's duration and expected end date.-  Combines these results with the farmer's own soil and irrigation data into a downloadable PDF report. The impact AgroNasa gives farmers evidence-based planning support, helping them use water efficiently, protect soil health, and reduce climate risk. It lowers the barrier to precision agriculture using open NASA data. It is an orientation aid, not a replacement for local agronomists.
details: Technical Details What it does It analyzes a farm plot using real climate and satellite data and recommends how suitable a crop is, which rotation strategy fits the farmer's priorities, and when the crop cycle would end. How it works The user selects a location and crop. The app queries NASA POWER for daily rainfall, temperature, and soil moisture, and compares the recent period with a configurable historical average. A scoring model rates climate fit, rotation, water, soil, and erosion, ranks the alternatives, and generates a PDF report that includes the farmer's own field data. Benefits- Free, open data and no installation: it runs in any browser.- Clear, explainable scores instead of black-box advice.- Saves water and protects soil through informed rotation choices.- A shareable PDF report for each analysis. Tech stack and resources- Front end: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Leaflet for maps and jsPDF for reports.- NASA data: NASA POWER API (climate and soil moisture) and NASA GIBS satellite layers (MODIS NDVI and surface temperature, SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG precipitation).- Other sources: Esri World Imagery, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and the FAO Crop Calendar.- ChatGPT was used to create the logo.- Claude and ChatGPT helped us write the code.- HeyGen was used to translate the video.
